title: AI Promo Video Maker for New Products | AIVideosUGC
description: Use this AI promo video maker to announce a new product with a warm, polished clip. Upload one photo, choose 9:16 or 1:1, and make your launch video today.
h1: AI Promo Video Maker for Your Next Product Launch
lead: Create a short product-launch video from a clear photo. Choose a creator review, unboxing, try-on or hands-on demo, then add the verified release date and offer after download.
intro: A launch video can introduce an item with a creator review, product demo, unboxing, try-on or first-bite reaction. Keep the featured product visible from the opening frame.
Use 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 1:1 for feeds and listings, or 16:9 for a wide placement. Add the confirmed date, price and product link as editable text after generation.

Launch content should make a new product feel ready to meet its first customer. Open with a creator holding the amber bottle, then show one drop or one clear product action in bright bathroom light. Keep the item visible from the first frame so a viewer understands what is being introduced before the launch date or message is added in the editor.

Plan the launch story around one proof point: the package silhouette, the way the dropper works, the first use, or a concise creator explanation. Use a single movement and a settled ending so the same source photo can support a teaser, a launch-day post, and a product-page image. Dates, availability, price, and claims should remain editable and tied to the information you can verify.

Before publishing, check that the image, product page, and stock record refer to the same item and variant. Adapt the composition for the chosen feed while protecting the face and bottle from interface overlays. A small set of launch hooks is easier to review when the scene, product, and destination stay fixed and only the opening line changes.

Treat the opening frame as the introduction. Show the new package, garment, or device before the creator begins the review, then use one reveal or one hand movement to establish what is new. A stable final frame gives the editor a place for the release date and product link.

Choose the channel before writing the scene. A [product launch occasion](/occasions/product-launch) keeps the release plan together, while [Instagram ads](/platforms/instagram-ads) and [YouTube Shorts ads](/platforms/youtube-shorts-ads) call for different crops. Use an [unboxing video](/ai-video-generation/unboxing-experience) when the package is part of the announcement and a [product video](/ai-video-generation/product-video) when the item itself needs a closer demonstration.

For a launch sequence, test a [UGC ad video](/ai-video-generation/ugc-ad-video) for a creator introduction, a [lifestyle scene](/ai-image-generation/lifestyle-scene) for the product page, and the [holiday occasion](/occasions/holidays) when gift timing is part of the plan. The [testing ad versions guide](/guides/testing-ad-versions) helps compare openings while the date, offer, and URL stay accurate.
tip: Choose one clear product moment, such as holding a bottle toward the camera, opening a gift box or showing a new item in use. Keep final launch facts editable.

faq.q: Should I make a square or a vertical version?
faq.a: Vertical 9:16 fills the screen in Stories and Reels, and square 1:1 sits neatly in the feed. You can make one of each. Every version is its own run, with the cost shown before it starts.

faq.q: Can I make a promo before my product photos are ready?
faq.a: You can start from a text description alone, but the product won't match your real one. For an ad, wait until you have a clear photo of the final item so shoppers see what they'll actually get.

faq.q: What length should a launch promo use?
faq.a: Use 6 seconds for a quick reveal, 10 or 15 seconds for a product action, and 30 seconds only where the public option is available. Choose 9:16 for vertical placements.

faq.q: Which ratio is best for launch day?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for TikTok and Reels, and a 1:1 version for feeds and listings. Both come from the same source photo.

faq.q: Can I make teaser content before stock arrives?
faq.a: Yes. Use a clear product photo to make a coming-soon clip, and add the date as editable text.

faq.q: What does a launch clip cost?
faq.a: A 6-, 10-, or 15-second clip is 24, 40, or 60 credits.

faq.q: What belongs in a launch teaser?
faq.a: Show the product and the reveal, then add the planned date as editable text so the teaser can be updated.

faq.q: How is a teaser different from release-day creative?
faq.a: A teaser can say coming soon; release-day creative should show the live date, current offer, and the product link.

faq.q: Where should I put the launch discount?
faq.a: Add the approved price or discount as an editable layer in a clear area after download and verify it on a phone preview.

faq.q: What should I check before publishing?
faq.a: Confirm the product shape, launch date, price, stock status, link, and crop in the final placement.

steps.sourceTitle: Creator holding an amber serum bottle
steps.sourceHint: Show the amber bottle and blank label clearly before adding the launch message.
steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the exact product: an amber glass dropper bottle with a black pipette and blank white label. Preserve its shape, glass color, cap and label area. In a bright bathroom, an adult creator holds the bottle beside her face and says, "Here is the serum I am showing today." She tilts the bottle once and finishes with the full bottle beside her cheek. Soft morning window light, natural skin texture. Chest-up front-facing framing with slight handheld sway. Sound: her voice and a cap click; no music.

cards.label: Creator Review: Espresso Maker
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a compact plain espresso maker and keep its controls and body visible. An adult presenter holds it at chest height while introducing the product in a bright kitchen. Creator launch review photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Kinetic Reveal: Cobalt Mug
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain cobalt-blue ceramic travel mug with its fitted lid and handle visible. Two adult hands pull cream paper wrap open as the mug is revealed on a sunlit table, creating a small kinetic launch moment. Product-launch reveal still, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Multi-Angle Hero: Olive Backpack

Show a multi-angle launch hero with the front three-quarter view large and smaller side and back views arranged behind it on studio plinths. Clean product-launch still, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: First Sip Reaction: Speckled Mug
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain speckled ceramic mug and keep its handle and flecked glaze visible. An older Black man holds the mug with both hands after a first sip in a bright kitchen, giving a clear launch reaction. UGC first-impression photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Try-On Transition: trail sneakers on walk
cards.prompt: Photorealistic square sportswear ad still: an adult runner wears charcoal trail sneakers with subtle orange trim on a city path, both shoes fully visible. Cool morning daylight, low close framing, natural pavement detail. Freeze a planted step. No text, logos, or watermark.

cards.label: Pet Demo: harness on dog
cards.prompt: Photorealistic square pet-product ad still: an adult owner checks the fit of a simple harness on a calm dog in a bright living room. Show the buckle and the dog’s full upper body clearly. Natural window light, medium close framing. Freeze the fit-check moment. No text, logos, or watermark.

cards.label: Hand Wash Routine: Dispenser
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a clear plain hand soap dispenser and keep its pump and bottle visible. A hand presses the dispenser over an open palm at a bathroom vanity, showing a simple daily routine. Routine launch photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Phone Audio Review: Earbuds
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain open matte-black wireless-earbud case and keep both earbuds visible. An older South Asian woman holds the case toward camera while explaining her first impression in a tidy home office. Creator review photo, square framing, no text or logos.
